counterfactual_missing_items: evidence of a primary malignancy on staging CT
history of smoking or known malignancy
decisive_items: CT of the thoracic spine showed an expansile bony lesion of the T1 vertebral body with extension into the left pedicle and posterior elements
CT scans of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis revealed no evidence of a primary malignancy
laboratory studies, including inflammatory markers, were within normal limits
response.rationale: R6 best matches the raw evidence: an expansile T1 vertebral body lesion with no primary malignancy on staging CT and normal inflammatory markers, favoring a primary spinal tumor. R1's metastatic label is contradicted by the absence of a primary; R2 is contradicted by normal labs; R4 and C1 describe only cord compression; R7 is too nonspecific.

rejected.why: Metastatic label is contradicted by the absence of a primary malignancy on staging CT.
Epidural abscess is contradicted by normal inflammatory markers and lack of infectious symptoms.
Spinal cord compression is a complication, not the underlying diagnosis.
Thoracic spine lesion is too nonspecific and does not consider the primary vs metastatic distinction.
Append-only completion of R4; still only localizes compression and does not identify the cause.
